findings.title: Stop and container-side AsyncListener events end the AsyncContext without marking the exchange aborted, so a drain thread can keep writing to a completed (possibly recycled) response
findings.description: Pool.completeAll() calls ex.complete() (ac.complete()) but never sets ServletExchange.aborted; FlushingStream.write/flush only fail once aborted is true (ServletExchange.check, line 387-391). After completeAll() the still-running drain keeps writing events/heartbeats through the old response output stream until shutdownNow() interrupts it, and a write that is not blocked/interruptible (heartbeat tick racing the stop) goes to a response the container has completed and may already have recycled for another connection (Jetty/Tomcat recycle request/response objects). The same gap exists in the AsyncListener of track(): onError/onTimeout only remove the exchange from the set; they neither complete the context (the Servlet 3.1 contract expects the app to complete or dispatch) nor flag the exchange, so the drain continues on a dead response and holds its SSE slot until the next write throws. Only abort() (aborted=true then complete()) is safe; completeAll and the listener bypass it.
findings.suggested_fix: In completeAll() call ex.abort() instead of ex.complete() (sets aborted first, then completes once). In the AsyncListener onError/onTimeout call ex.abort() so the next FlushingStream write throws IOException and the drain ends and releases the slot. Add a test that a write after completeAll() throws IOException.

findings.title: ServletRegistration.Dynamic.addMapping result is ignored: a conflicting url-pattern silently leaves the started app unreachable
findings.description: addMapping(String...) returns the set of patterns that were NOT mapped because another servlet already owns them (typical for "/" against a container default servlet registration, or "/api/*" against an existing mapping). register() discards the return value, so context startup succeeds, listen(0) has run, onStart callbacks fired, but the servlet receives no request. The operator sees a healthy app that answers 404 from the container. The other failure paths in this class (name clash, bad init-param) are all turned into a ServletException with app shutdown, so this one is inconsistent with the design's fail-fast startup.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the returned Collection<String>; if it is non-empty throw new ServletException("naruserve.urlPattern '" + pattern + "' conflicts with an existing mapping") so the surrounding catch shuts the app down. Add a test registering a second servlet on the same pattern.

findings.title: AppStarter error wrapping is incomplete: Errors from configure() escape unnamed, and a failing GsonJsonCodec constructor is reported as an absent codec
findings.description: (a) The Javadoc and IR-SVL-001 AC-6 promise every configure failure is a ServletException naming the class, but only Exception is caught (line 66); a NoClassDefFoundError/LinkageError thrown by the configurer body (e.g. a missing optional dependency, the most common real deployment failure) propagates raw without the configurer class name. (b) presetCodec catches ReflectiveOperationException, so an InvocationTargetException from a throwing GsonJsonCodec constructor is swallowed and returns false; if the configurer then does not set a codec the message tells the user to put GsonJsonCodec on the class path although it is there and failed. (c) The no-codec hint depends on the substring "jsonCodec" in RestApp.Builder.build()'s IllegalStateException message (RestApp.java:261), a silent coupling with no shared constant.
findings.suggested_fix: Catch LinkageError in the configure try block and wrap it like the Exception branch; in presetCodec rethrow or log the InvocationTargetException cause (keep returning false only for ClassNotFoundException/NoClassDefFoundError); note the message coupling in a test that fails if the core message changes.

findings.title: shutdownTimeoutSeconds accepts forms the SRS does not intend because Integer.parseInt is used on the raw text
findings.description:
IR-SVL-001 AC-5 specifies an integer from 1 to 300; Integer.parseInt also accepts a leading '+' ("+5") and non-ASCII Unicode digits, while rejecting surrounding whitespace that web.xml authors commonly produce (<param-value>
 30
</param-value>), which then fails startup with a message naming the value. Behavior is inconsistent: some non-canonical forms pass, the most likely one does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Either trim() the value before parsing, or match against "[0-9]{1,3}" first so only canonical digits pass; document the choice in docs/api/servlet.md.
